QR Code Best Practices - Expert Guide

📏 Size Matters for Print

For printed materials, ensure QR codes are at least 2x2cm (0.8x0.8 inches) for reliable scanning. Larger is better for ease of use. Test with actual smartphones before mass printing.

🎨 Maintain High Contrast

Use dark colors (black, dark blue) on light backgrounds (white, yellow). Avoid low-contrast combinations that make scanning difficult. Our default black-and-white QR codes offer maximum reliability.

🔍 Quiet Zone is Essential

Maintain clear space around the QR code (at least 4 times the size of a single module). This 'quiet zone' ensures scanners can distinguish the QR code from surrounding content.

📱 Test on Multiple Devices

Verify your QR code scans correctly with various smartphones (iPhone, Android) and scanning apps before deployment. What works on one device may not work on another.

🌐 Shorten Long URLs

For very long URLs, consider using URL shorteners first. Shorter URLs create simpler QR codes with larger modules, improving scan reliability and allowing smaller print sizes.

🎯 Clear Call-to-Action

Always include text near your QR code explaining what users will get by scanning (e.g., 'Scan to visit our website' or 'Scan for exclusive offer'). This increases scan rates significantly.
